events.title: Administrative Stay in Danco Laboratories, LLC v. Louisiana, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States issued an administrative stay on the May 1, 2026 order of the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit in case No. 26-30203. This stay is effective until 5 p.m. (EDT) on May 11, 2026. Additionally, the Court ordered that a response to the application be filed by 5 p.m. (EDT) on May 7, 2026. The order was signed by Associate Justice Samuel A. Alito, Jr.
events.why_relevant: The administrative stay temporarily halts the lower court's order, affecting the immediate legal proceedings and timelines.

events.title: Administrative Stay in GenBioPro, Inc. v. Louisiana, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States issued an administrative stay on the May 1, 2026 order from the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit in the case of GenBioPro, Inc. v. Louisiana, et al. (No. 25A1208). The stay is effective until 5 p.m. (EDT) on May 11, 2026. Additionally, the Court ordered that a response to the application be filed by May 7, 2026, at 5 p.m. (EDT). This order was signed by Associate Justice Samuel A. Alito, Jr.
events.why_relevant: The administrative stay temporarily halts the enforcement of a lower court's decision, affecting the legal proceedings and potential outcomes in this case.

events.title: Bell v. Swift
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the motion for leave to proceed in forma pauperis and dismissed the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Bell, Andrew W. v. Swift, Karli, et al. (Docket No. 25-6970).
events.why_relevant: This dismissal affects the petitioner's ability to have their case heard by the Supreme Court.

events.title: Jacquett v. Jacquett
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the motion for leave to proceed as a veteran in the case of Jacquett, Taron v. Jacquett, Estefania (Docket No. 25M70).
events.why_relevant: This denial affects the procedural status of the case, impacting the petitioner's ability to proceed under veteran status.

events.title: Johnson v. New Jersey
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the motion for reconsideration of an order denying leave to proceed in forma pauperis in the case of Johnson, Naquea E. v. New Jersey, et al. (Docket No. 25-6617).
events.why_relevant: This denial impacts the petitioner's ability to proceed without financial burden, affecting access to justice.

events.title: Mundi v. Superior Court of CA
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the motions for leave to proceed in forma pauperis in the cases of Mundi, Mandeep v. Superior Court of CA, et al. (Docket No. 25-6951) and others, requiring petitioners to pay docketing fees by May 26, 2026.
events.why_relevant: This decision imposes financial requirements on petitioners, potentially limiting access to the Court.

events.title: Tootle v. Bohinski
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the motion to direct the Clerk to file a petition for a writ of certiorari out of time in the case of Tootle, Brian v. Bohinski, Supt., Dallas, et al. (Docket No. 25M71).
events.why_relevant: This denial prevents the petitioner from pursuing a late appeal, affecting their access to the Court.

events.title: Invitation for Amicus Curiae in Beaird v. United States
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States has invited Anthony J. Dick, Esquire, to brief and argue the case of Beaird v. United States as amicus curiae. The invitation is to support the position that the precedent set in Stinson v. United States, which addresses the deference courts must give to the commentary on the Sentencing Guidelines, remains valid. This procedural action indicates the Court's interest in examining the continued applicability of this legal standard.
events.why_relevant: The invitation for amicus curiae participation suggests the Court's willingness to reconsider or affirm the legal standards governing judicial deference to sentencing guidelines.
